head: 4b382e5388e652308d2beca448666630ba6c332d
summary: Shaka replaces a misleading JSON error with a lookup failure and preserves HTTP status internally. The bounded implementation leaves the promised diagnosis unavailable in user-facing output.
reasons: The change stays within the planned two files and reuses existing error handling without new dependencies or configuration. One review round provides no evidence of approach churn; incident frequency and time saved remain unknown.

Reported verification includes the failing-then-passing reproduction, 3454 passing tests, clean RuboCop, and a live missing-PR lookup. This is proportionate to a reversible diagnostic change, but does not demonstrate the promised user-visible rate-limit diagnosis.
No instructions changed, so instruction-growth evidence does not affect this assessment.
concerns: The intended audience still cannot distinguish rate limiting from other lookup failures. check_list.rb preserves HTTP status as exception metadata, but status.rb retains only the generic required-check message, and scripts/shaka.rb and pr_watch/command.rb print only e.message. The promised HTTP status and rate-limit cause do not reach those outputs.

The supplied verification does not exercise rate-limit diagnostics through pr, pr watch, handoff, or merge. A live rate limit was not triggered; GraphQL messages without '(HTTP nnn)' still yield no status.
alternative: Retain this narrow fix and expose a sanitized HTTP status through the existing command and check-evidence outputs. Preserve fail-closed behavior and stderr privacy. A generic failure message is simpler, but loses the requested diagnostic distinction; no evidence establishes that loss as acceptable.
next_action: Revise this PR to carry sanitized HTTP status into command and check-evidence output, then verify a simulated HTTP 403 through those boundaries.
